I've been saving up quite some time to purchase my own gun. Yes my state allows you to own semi-auto.

One of the things I've been wondering is which particular model of the AR-15 is a decent choice for it's price? I've seen a "pistol" version and a rifle version, and several variations of the latter.

On top of that I'm trying to decide on a pistol as well. So far I've heard good things about any 9mm Glock, 9mm 1911, and Sigs. My friend has a USP and it seemed to handle well but I'm no expert.

Again I'm really looking for best bang for the buck. Something that will last a long time, reliable, easy maintenance. Power isn't really a concern of mine.

EDIT: Thanks for the replies it's helped me narrow my search by a lot.

I should clarify a few things:

  • I have had training with firearms
  • I'm looking to get a CWP after I've chosen a gun I'm comfortable with
  • I prefer handguns that aren't too heavy (.45 1911 and some sigs have felt heavy to me when I held them)
  • I prefer 9mm over .45 but open to suggestions
Looking for advice on which guns suite me best.

For the rifle, I suggest the Smith and Wesson M & P 15 Sport II. This is the optimal level of quality and low price you can get in an AR-15. What you lose at this price is some of the fluff (like a case to put it in) and some of the ability to customize it (since rail space is sparse.) Here is a review.

As for a handgun, I'm not a glock fan. I like my m9a1 Beretta. Glock is still a good choice. Sig is a good choice. A heavy 1911 frame will make shooting it a breeze if you go that way. What you need to do there is try out a few and see which works for you. The 1911 will be pricier, but for a quality pistol in 9mm, you will end up dropping between 550 and 700. Find something in that range that feels good to hold and shoot. I suggest you go to a range and try out a few of them with a rental. Most of the time you can change them out with a single rental fee.

If they're lucky there's hopefully a gunshop/range combo in their area. There's one about 30 minutes from me and it's more or less the place to go when buying your first gun since you can very easily try it out on the spot with little issue.

If you're on the handy side of things you can also buy a stripped lower and a parts kit and assemble an AR-15 yourself. Probably not any cheaper in the long run, but it gives you a better understanding of how the gun works and how the pieces fit together.

As far as handguns go - just get a 9mm that fits your hand like pcdude suggests. Glocks aren't for everyone but I like my 19 a lot.

Ok... just to cover the basics (since you're asking rather basic questions), have you had ANY formal training? If not, then that is your first course of action. Please, for the love of any and everything you hold dear, educate yourself first. During that education (likely different classes for the different firearm types) you ought to be allowed/encouraged to shoot a variety.

Past that, "best" is entirely personal. If you're not comfortable with, and don't like shooting a .45 but Are comfortable with and enjoy shooting a .22... that means the .22 is a better option. You say you want the "best bang for the buck", and that is, absolutely, without ANY debate, a .22lr, especially when you claim that power isn't a concern. Actually, there may be air rifles that are even cheaper (I only know super high-end airgun stuff, my Steyr LP10 air pistol is a $2000 tool), the ammo certainly is and you can shoot them most places legally and Everywhere with a little common sense... I have an indoor range from my bedroom down the hall. :)

Anyway, not thinking about power and wanting just best bang for the buck, .22lr ~ the ammo is cheap ($0.07 per round) when compared to the cheapest handgun alternative (9mm @ $0.16 per round) and rifle (.223 @ $0.21 per round). That's 2 to 3 times as many rounds fired for the same ammo cost. Then you have Purchase price, the .22lr pistols (Sig Mosquito, Walther PPQ 22, Rugers, etc...) all run about $300~350 while the 9mm equivalents run from $450~$1000 (or more). Rifles are the same story, if you want the 'black gun' look then the Smith and Wesson M&P15-22 is the most available option out there and runs $350. The cheapest AR-15 platform, even used, is closer to $600.

Between the 2 you'd probably be spending ~$300 less by going with high end .22lr options vs the Cheapest upscale alternatives, which is about 5000 rounds of .22lr (that Both firearms can shoot, there's a lot to be said for minimizing your ammo stock).

Beyond that, if you're itching to spend more money, then you really need to test out the different firearms, especially the pistols. The AR platform is the AR platform. There's very little difference, and I'd hazard to say NONE that a new shooter would recognize. But with pistols you have 4 major sizes (pocket, sub-compact, compact, full size), with different ideologies (single action only, double action only, single-double, striker fired), and heck even different magazine layouts (single stack and double-stack). Grip angles change your natural point of aim, some sights (stock, all of them can be changed for more $$$) work better for some people... I love Steyr sights.

Then you can think about use. If you're going to open or conceal carry the pistol, Ever. Is it just a range gun? Are you looking to plink with friends are do you want to compete?

Anyway, it's not just a "Brand X is best" thing. ALL the major brands offer phenomenal equipment that could easily last several generations of use. The important variable is you, what you want to use the firearm for, what fits you best. You only get that knowledge through experience.

Good luck from a USAS/NRA cert. coach
